title: New York City · Layers.City
heading: New York City
description: A map of New York City with toggleable layers: the five boroughs, 59 community districts and 2020 neighborhood tabulation areas, known-as names, City Council, State Assembly and Senate and congressional districts, landmarks, historic districts, main streets, highways, the subway, and the commuter trains of the tri-state region, who represents each spot and where to vote on November 3.
attribution: Boroughs, community districts, NTAs, council, Assembly, Senate, congressional and school districts: NYC Department of City Planning · Historic districts: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission · Business improvement districts: NYC Small Business Services · Subway, LIRR & Metro-North: MTA GTFS · Towns and counties around the city & ACS figures: U.S. Census Bureau · Skyscrapers: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA) · NJ Transit & PATH lines, streets, highways & address search: © OpenStreetMap contributors via Nominatim · Poll sites: NYC Board of Elections; positions: NYS GIS Program Office · Representatives: Open States, Clerk of the U.S. House, NYC Council · Buses: MTA GTFS · Bike lanes: NYC DOT · Citi Bike stations: Lyft (Citi Bike data policy) · Landmarks: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission · Tree cover: ESA WorldCover 2021 (CC BY 4.0) · Drive times: OSRM on OpenStreetMap · Collection days: NYC Department of Sanitation · Parks, playgrounds, pools and courts: NYC Parks · Hospitals, colleges, libraries, schools and older adult centers: NYC Department of City Planning Facilities Database · Street closures: NYC Department of Transportation; special events: NYC permitted events and street centerline · New development: NYC Department of Buildings (DOB NOW), rezonings: NYC Department of City Planning (ZAP, PLUTO) · Ferries: NYC Ferry and NYC DOT timetables (GTFS) · Congestion Relief Zone: drawn from the MTA’s description (60th Street and south) · Hurricane evacuation zones and centers: NYC Emergency Management · Places of worship & lines being built: © OpenStreetMap contributors · Municipal parking: NYC DOT · EV chargers: U.S. DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center · Halal & kosher shops: NYS Department of Agriculture and Markets registries

facts.label: Congestion toll
facts.text: Inside the Congestion Relief Zone: driving in costs $9 a day for a car at peak times with E-ZPass, less at night (2026; the FDR Drive and West Side Highway are toll-free)

living.caveat: Survey estimates for 2020–2024, not current prices, for the whole community district. Rent is what renting households pay, utilities included, counting rent-stabilized and subsidized homes, so it sits well below what a new lease costs. Use them to compare districts, not to budget.

address.label: Address
address.sub: Numbered streets take East or West ({street}) and count up away from Fifth Avenue; avenues count up going north.

elsewhere.Queens: Hyphenated numbers: in 37-18 82nd St, “37” is the nearest cross street (37th Ave) and “18” the house on that block.
elsewhere.Bronx: Jerome Avenue splits the Bronx’s streets into East and West (E 167th St, W 167th St).
elsewhere.Brooklyn: No borough-wide grid: each street counts up from its own start, usually nearest the East River or the harbor.
elsewhere.Staten Island: No grid: each street counts up from its own start.

transit.title: Transit nearby
transit.every: about every {h} min on weekday middays
transit.note: Routes with a stop within 400 m, about a 5-minute walk. Numbers with a double ring come every 10 minutes or better on weekdays. Tap a number to draw the route. MTA schedules, week of {week}; Citi Bike’s station list.

pickup.label: Collection day
pickup.head: Trash {r} · recycling {y}[ · compost {o}]
pickup.outside: Not on DSNY’s curbside schedule here.
pickup.note: DSNY collection days for this section; set your trash out after 8 pm the night before. Holidays can move a day: check DSNY’s collection schedule lookup.

nearby.note: Straight-line distances; half a mile is about a 10-minute walk. NYC Parks, the three public library systems and the City’s Facilities Database. Counts parks, not courts. Evacuation centers from NYC Emergency Management: they open only when the City orders an evacuation. Schools are NYC Public Schools; zoning depends on the address, not distance. Places of worship (OpenStreetMap) show while their layer is on.
nearby.sources: Sources: NYC Parks, the three public library systems, the City's Facilities Database, NYC Emergency Management (evacuation centers), NYC Public Schools, OpenStreetMap (places of worship), New York State (certified kosher and halal shops).

schools.title: Schools
schools.note: The NYC Public Schools zoned for this spot, from the DOE’s {year} school zones. Distances are straight-line to the building. Zones change and some schools have more applicants than seats; the DOE’s school search has the final word.

changes.title: Changing nearby
changes.none: Nothing big proposed, approved, under way or finished within ½ mile in the last two years.
changes.more: And {n} more nearby: turn on New development to see them.
changes.note: Land-use applications are proposals, not decisions; an area rezoning is placed at the middle of its lots. Big changes within ½ mile: rezonings, new buildings and demolitions, no one- or two-family houses. NYC Department of City Planning (ZAP) and Department of Buildings (DOB NOW), as of {date}.

closures.note: Closures for rapid transit construction within ½ mile only; other street work isn’t shown. Dates are permit dates, not a forecast of when the street reopens. NYC DOT, as of {date}.

steps.title: Five boroughs
steps.text: New York City is five boroughs, each also a county: Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island. Only the Bronx is on the mainland; Brooklyn and Queens sit on Long Island.

steps.title: Community districts and the names people say
steps.text: The city is split into 59 community districts, each with a community board that weighs in on zoning and services. The names in italics are what people actually say: SoHo, DUMBO, Hell’s Kitchen.

steps.title: Getting around
steps.text: The subway runs around the clock. Commuter trains fan out from Penn Station and Grand Central: the LIRR to Long Island, Metro-North to Westchester and Connecticut, NJ Transit and PATH across the Hudson.

steps.title: Tap anywhere
steps.text: Tap any spot or search an address, and the card shows the borough, community district and neighborhood it’s in, what living there is like, and its council, state and congressional districts.
